evidence_spans.text: we observe a striking enrichment of the transcriptional co-activator p300 (3.3-fold enrichment; p = 2.0E-0004, Wilcoxon)

These results suggest that Mosaic-seq can robustly and specifically detect changes in gene expression induced by epigenome engineering of single cells in a manner that is consistent with traditional approaches.
HS2 exhibited the most robust repression, triggering an 86.2% loss of HBG2 expression

Overall, we find that these constituents have a widely variable effect on gene expression when averaged across cells, ranging from 18.0% to 88.9%, with a median of 42.3%. In contrast, most constituents tested elicit no detectable changes in expression, suggesting that they only contribute weakly to gene expression, at least when studied in isolation with KRAB.
repression of SE2 HS2, on average, caused an 88.9% loss of PIM1 expression
Recruitment of dCas9-KRAB to HBG1/2 promoters caused a single-cell median expression decrease of >97.3%
we estimate that the sgRNA barcode contamination rate is only 0.83% of barcode reads
We identified 12 constituent enhancers targeted by at least two sgRNAs that repressed target genes in the same TAD by at least 10%
Each enhancer was targeted by two to four sgRNAs in an average of 465.6 cells.
Recruitment of KRAB to the HS2 enhancer causes robust repression (>91.7%) of HBG1/2 and HBE1 in single cells

These observations suggest that simultaneous repression of multiple weak constituents can robustly alter super-enhancer activity and that it does so in a manner that is significantly greater than the repression of individual constituents.
we estimate that the sgRNA barcode contamination rate is only 0.83% of barcode reads
For each of the 36 pairwise combinations of two sgRNAs (excluding HS2), we sequenced a median of 154 cells
50% of the pairwise sgRNA combinations exhibited significant (p < 0.001, hypergeometric) loss of PIM1 expression
we observe a striking enrichment of the transcriptional co-activator p300 (3.3-fold enrichment; p = 2.0E-0004, Wilcoxon) and RNA polymerase II (RNAPII) (3.4-fold; p = 0.0047, Wilcoxon).

limitations.statement: Unknown whether KRAB is a universal repressor of all enhancers; false negatives possible (page 14).
Mosaic-seq relies on antibiotic selection, limiting application to proliferating cells (page 14).
Cannot distinguish primary enhancer targets from downstream secondary effects (page 14).
Due to detection limits of scRNA-seq, applying to enhancers regulating lowly expressed genes likely requires more reads or cells (page 14).
Mosaic-seq is about 83x more expensive than high-throughput reporter assays, limiting genome-wide application until sequencing costs decrease (page 14).
